stem: FDA guidance recommends avoiding systemic NSAIDs at 30 weeks of pregnancy and later because of which additional fetal risk?

options.A: Premature closure of the fetal ductus arteriosus
options.B: Delayed closure of the fetal neural tube
options.C: Permanent opening of the fetal foramen ovale

rationale: FDA recommends limiting NSAID use between 20 and 30 weeks because of fetal renal dysfunction and oligohydramnios risk and avoiding NSAIDs at 30 weeks and later because of the additional risk of premature closure of the fetal ductus arteriosus. Therefore A is correct. The other choices are not the FDA-described reason for the 30-week threshold.
educational_objective: Distinguish the FDA NSAID pregnancy risks by gestational timing: renal dysfunction/oligohydramnios from about 20 weeks and premature ductus arteriosus closure at 30 weeks and later.
source_document_title: FDA recommends avoiding use of NSAIDs in pregnancy at 20 weeks or later because they can result in low amniotic fluid
source_version_date: FDA Drug Safety Communication issued 2020-10-15; updated 2022-09-01; current page accessed 2026-08-17

source_claim_supported: At 30 weeks of pregnancy and later, NSAIDs carry the additional risk of premature closure of the fetal ductus arteriosus.

correction_summary: Corrected the source item's conflation of the 20-week renal/oligohydramnios warning with the 30-week ductus-closure warning. Reframed the stem around the exact FDA 30-week threshold and removed vague 'third trimester' wording.
audit_findings: A exactly matches FDA guidance. B, C and D are not FDA-described NSAID fetal risks at this threshold. The stem specifies 'additional' risk at 30 weeks, preventing the 20-week renal-risk fact from becoming a second defensible answer. No unresolved conflict or unsupported precision remains.
